title: えきの ねこ
img: A tiny rural Japanese train station at golden evening light, a wooden platform with a small bench and potted flowers, a fluffy orange-and-white cat bounding joyfully toward a young schoolgirl with a backpack who has just stepped off a two-car local train, the girl kneeling with arms open and a big smile, rice fields and distant green hills behind, long warm shadows and a pink-orange sky, a feeling of a happy homecoming. Painted in a consistent warm, hand-painted Studio-Ghibli-inspired watercolor style: soft edges, gentle textured paper, rich but soft colors, cozy nostalgic atmosphere. No text, letters, signs with writing, or captions anywhere in the image.

sents.en: There is a cat at a small station.
The cat's name is Tama.
Every day, Tama waits for the train in front of the station.
In the evening, a train comes.
A girl gets off the train.
"Tama, I'm home!"
Tama runs over to the girl.
Tama wasn't waiting for the train, but for this girl.

qs.q: ねこの なまえは なんですか。
qs.qen: What is the cat's name?

qs.q: でんしゃは いつ きますか。
qs.qen: When does the train come?

qs.q: タマは だれを まって いましたか。
qs.qen: Who was Tama waiting for?

sents.en: Today it is raining.
I go into a small café.
I order coffee and cake.
Outside the window, there is a man with no umbrella.
There are two umbrellas in my bag.
I go outside and say, "Here, take this."
The man smiles and says, "Thank you."
On the next rainy day, that man came to the café carrying the umbrella and a cake.

qs.q: わたしは カフェで なにを たのみましたか。
qs.qen: What did I order at the café?

qs.q: つぎの あめの ひ、おとこのひとは なにを もって きましたか。

sents.en: Today I made onigiri with Grandma.
Grandma's onigiri were neat triangles.
My onigiri were round and a little oddly shaped.
We put pickled plums inside.
Grandma ate my onigiri.
"Delicious! This is the most delicious one!"
I was very happy.
Tomorrow, I will make onigiri for Grandma.

qs.qen: What shape were Grandma's onigiri?

title: 新しい 学校
img: A bright Tokyo classroom at lunchtime in spring, cherry blossom petals drifting past large windows with a view of city rooftops, two schoolgirls in navy sailor uniforms sitting at pushed-together desks laughing with delight as they compare their open bento boxes, each containing an identical cat-shaped onigiri with nori ears and whiskers, soft dappled sunlight, fresh and joyful first-day-of-friendship mood. Painted in a consistent warm, hand-painted Studio-Ghibli-inspired watercolor style: soft edges, gentle textured paper, rich but soft colors, cozy nostalgic atmosphere. No text, letters, signs with writing, or captions anywhere in the image.

sents.en: Today is my first day at a new school in Tokyo.
My heart had been pounding since the morning.

tok.s: ドキドキしていました

sents.en: In the classroom there were lots of people I didn't know.
The girl next to me said, "Good morning."
Her name is Yui.
At lunch break, the two of us ate our bento.
In Yui's bento there was a cat-shaped onigiri.
And in my bento, too, there was a cat onigiri!
"They're the same!"
The two of us laughed a lot.
We quickly became friends.
I'm looking forward to going to school tomorrow, too.

qs.q: 「わたし」の 新しい 学校は どこに ありますか。
qs.qen: Where is the narrator's new school?

title: あおい かさ
img: A small Japanese train station office window at dusk just after the rain, the wet platform glistening with reflections of warm station lights, a kind uniformed station attendant smiling beside a little girl in a yellow raincoat and red boots who proudly holds out a bright blue umbrella to a grateful young office worker in a suit, puddles shimmering, clouds parting to show a soft peach sky, gentle heartwarming mood. Painted in a consistent warm, hand-painted Studio-Ghibli-inspired watercolor style: soft edges, gentle textured paper, rich but soft colors, cozy nostalgic atmosphere. No text, letters, signs with writing, or captions anywhere in the image.

sents.en: On Monday morning, it was raining.
I got on the train holding a blue umbrella.
That umbrella was a present from my father.
I got off the train at the station where my company is.
But I left my umbrella on the train!

tok.s: わすれてしまいました

sents.en: All day long, I kept thinking about the umbrella.
At five o'clock, I asked a station worker.
"A blue umbrella, right? We have it."
The station worker came with a little girl.
The girl had found the umbrella and kindly brought it to the station.
I said "Thank you" to the girl.
Outside, the rain had already stopped.

qs.q: あおい かさは だれからの プレゼントでしたか。
qs.qen: Who was the blue umbrella a present from?

qs.q: 「わたし」は どこに かさを わすれましたか。
qs.qen: Where did the narrator leave the umbrella?

qs.q: だれが かさを 見つけましたか。
qs.qen: Who found the umbrella?

title: なつまつりの 金魚
img: A lively Japanese summer festival at night, rows of glowing paper lanterns strung above a street of food stalls, two young girls in colorful yukata (one with a morning-glory pattern, one with goldfish pattern) looking up in wonder at huge fireworks blooming in the dark blue sky, one girl holding up a clear plastic bag with a single little red goldfish that seems to gaze at the fireworks too, sparkling reflections of the fireworks in the water of the bag, festive, magical, nostalgic mood. Painted in a consistent warm, hand-painted Studio-Ghibli-inspired watercolor style: soft edges, gentle textured paper, rich but soft colors, cozy nostalgic atmosphere. No text, letters, signs with writing, or captions anywhere in the image.

sents.en: On a Saturday in August, I went to the summer festival with a friend.
I wore a yukata.
Lots of little stalls were lined up along the street.
We ate takoyaki and shaved ice.
After that, we did goldfish scooping.
I couldn't scoop even one.
But my friend scooped three.
My friend gave me one.
At nine at night, big fireworks went up.
The goldfish seemed to be watching the fireworks too.
Now that goldfish lives at my house.
Its name is "Hanabi" (Fireworks).

qs.q: なつまつりは いつでしたか。
qs.qen: When was the summer festival?

qs.q: 友だちは 金魚を 何びき すくいましたか。
qs.qen: How many goldfish did the friend scoop?

qs.q: 金魚の 名前は 何ですか。
qs.qen: What is the goldfish's name?

title: まよなかの コンビニ
img: A glowing Japanese convenience store at midnight on a cold winter street, bright white-and-warm light spilling from the big glass front onto a quiet snowy sidewalk; inside at the counter, a tired young clerk in a striped uniform receives a steaming meat bun from a kind elderly man in a flat cap and scarf who smiles warmly, a steamer case of buns glowing on the counter, soft steam rising, deep indigo night sky outside, tender and heartwarming mood. Painted in a consistent warm, hand-painted Studio-Ghibli-inspired watercolor style: soft edges, gentle textured paper, rich but soft colors, cozy nostalgic atmosphere. No text, letters, signs with writing, or captions anywhere in the image.

sents.en: I work part-time at a convenience store.
I work from ten at night until six in the morning.
At twelve midnight, an old man comes.
He always buys milk and one meat bun.
But today he bought two meat buns.
I said, "Two today, huh."
Then the old man gave me one meat bun.
"Thanks as always. Good luck with your night work."
The meat bun was very warm.
It was a cold night outside, but my heart became warm too.

qs.qen: What time does the old man come?

qs.q: おじいさんは いつも 何を 買いますか。
qs.qen: What does the old man always buy?

qs.qen: Why did he buy two meat buns today?

title: 京都で 道に まよって
img: A tiny hidden temple garden in Kyoto in late autumn, blazing red and orange maple leaves over a moss-covered stone path and a small weathered wooden temple hall, a lone young traveler with a backpack sitting quietly on the veranda gazing at the garden, fallen leaves on the mossy ground, soft slanting late-afternoon light filtering through the leaves, peaceful, secret, serene mood. Painted in a consistent warm, hand-painted Studio-Ghibli-inspired watercolor style: soft edges, gentle textured paper, rich but soft colors, cozy nostalgic atmosphere. No text, letters, signs with writing, or captions anywhere in the image.

sents.en: In autumn, I went on a trip to Kyoto by myself.
I was planning to go see a famous temple listed in my guidebook.
But while walking along narrow streets, I ended up getting lost.

tok.s: まよってしまいました

sents.en: Even looking at the map, I couldn't tell where I was.
Just then, an old woman from a small sweet shop called out to me.
"Where do you want to go?"
When I said the temple's name, she laughed and said, "There are a lot of people there today."
And then she told me about a small temple behind her shop.
There was no one there.
The maple leaves in the garden were bright red, and it was very quiet.
I sat there for a long time.
On the way back, I bought sweets at the old woman's shop.
I couldn't go to the famous temple, but that became my best memory.

qs.qen: Where was the narrator originally planning to go?

qs.q: 道に まよった 時、だれが 声を かけて くれましたか。
qs.qen: Who called out to the narrator when they got lost?

qs.qen: What was the small temple like?

title: 富士山の 日の出
img: The summit of Mt. Fuji at dawn, a father and his teenage child in hiking jackets and headlamps standing on dark volcanic rock above an endless sea of clouds glowing pink, orange and gold, the brilliant sun just breaking through a gap in the clouds, the father holding out a faded old photograph toward the child, other climbers silhouetted in the distance raising their arms, crisp cold air and a sense of awe and quiet emotion. Painted in a consistent warm, hand-painted Studio-Ghibli-inspired watercolor style: soft edges, gentle textured paper, rich but soft colors, cozy nostalgic atmosphere. No text, letters, signs with writing, or captions anywhere in the image.

sents.en: During summer vacation, I climbed Mt. Fuji with my father.
We left the mountain hut at two in the middle of the night and walked slowly along the dark path.
The air was thin, and I got very tired.
"Almost there," my father said again and again.
Around four-thirty in the morning, we finally reached the summit.
But the eastern sky was covered with thick clouds.
I was disappointed and looked down.
Just then, the people around us cried out, "Ah!"
A golden sun had come out from a gap in the clouds.
The sea of clouds was shining pink and orange.
My father took an old photo out of his pocket.
It was a photo of my father and mother, taken here thirty years ago.
"I proposed to your mom right here," my father said with a laugh.
This time, I was the one who took a photo of my father.

qs.q: 二人は 何時ごろ 頂上に 着きましたか。
qs.qen: Around what time did the two reach the summit?

qs.q: 頂上に 着いた 時、東の 空は どうでしたか。
qs.qen: When they reached the summit, what was the eastern sky like?
opts: 厚い 雲で おおわれていた

qs.qen: What was father's old photo?

title: 二十歳の わたしへ
img: A small desk by a window at night in a cozy Japanese apartment, a young woman of twenty sitting under a warm desk lamp drawing a cute cat in a new sketchbook with a pencil, beside her an old rust-spotted tin time-capsule box and an unfolded childhood letter covered in large clumsy handwriting shapes and a crayon cat doodle, a mug of tea steaming, city lights and a crescent moon outside, quiet, hopeful, nostalgic mood. Painted in a consistent warm, hand-painted Studio-Ghibli-inspired watercolor style: soft edges, gentle textured paper, rich but soft colors, cozy nostalgic atmosphere. No text, letters, signs with writing, or captions anywhere in the image.

sents.en: When I was ten, I wrote "A Letter to Myself Ten Years From Now" at school.
We put the letters in a time capsule and buried it in the schoolyard.
And this year, now twenty, we gathered at the school.
The box that came out of the ground was a little rusty.
The handwriting in my letter was big and clumsy.
"Dear me at twenty. Are you still drawing pictures?"
I couldn't answer.

tok.s: 答えられませんでした
tok.r: こたえられませんでした

sents.en: That's because after starting university, I got busy and quit drawing.
At the end of the letter, there was a clumsy drawing of a cat.
Under it was written, "Someday I want to make a cat book!"
On the way home, I bought a small notebook and a pencil at a shop in the station.
That night, I drew a cat for the first time in ten years.
And then I began writing a new letter to myself at thirty.
"Dear me at thirty. Is the cat book finished?"

qs.q: 手紙は どこに うめましたか。
qs.qen: Where was the letter buried?

qs.q: 「わたし」は どうして 絵を やめて しまいましたか。
qs.qen: Why did the narrator quit drawing?
opts: 大学に 入って いそがしかったから
絵が きらいに なったから
えんぴつが なかったから
先生に 言われたから

qs.q: 十歳の 「わたし」は いつか 何を 作りたかったですか。
qs.qen: What did the ten-year-old narrator want to make someday?
